name: Ban Non Wat early chicken remains
description: Chicken remains at Ban Non Wat in Thailand have been interpreted as an early population associated with human settlement.

impact.note: One site's remains witness early chicken keeping in a region the bird later spread from, but the reading is hedged, so scores stay low.

date.label: Approximately 1650–1250 BCE
date.basis: Approximate archaeological context; calibrated BP values use 1950 as reference.

events.statement: Chicken remains at Ban Non Wat in Thailand have been interpreted as an early population associated with human settlement.

evidence.supports: The authors describe abundant Gallus remains and juveniles in a site context around 1650–1250 BCE.

events.caveats: Chicken bones occur in the Neolithic site assemblage; the authors regard domestic status as unresolved. Later chicken burials date to later contexts. Presence does not prove husbandry, egg use or food use.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest supported event for this scoped case, not a universal priority claim. Domestic status remains unresolved according to the authors; later chicken burials belong to later contexts and no early food or egg use is established.
